hunks.baseline: It was so dark, with countless wrecks and corpses filling the water, that it was impossible to see even an inch ahead. Then, without warning, blue-white flames erupted.
hunks.sol: Countless wrecks and corpses darkened the water until it was impossible to see an inch ahead. Then blue-white flames erupted.

hunks.baseline: The current split apart, and the water vaporized.
hunks.sol: The current split, and the water vaporized.

hunks.baseline: The flames carried a force that defied the laws of nature. No—a spear shot forward like a ray of light.
hunks.sol: The flames carried an energy that defied the laws of nature. No—a spear shot forward like a ray of light.

hunks.baseline: But just as the force within the spear defied the laws of nature, so too did the mythical monster.
hunks.sol: But the mythical monster defied the laws of nature just as surely as the energy in the spear did.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, large and small whirlpools of water surged up from the depths and blocked the spearhead as it raced forward.
hunks.sol: Whirlpools large and small rose from the depths, blocking the spearhead as it raced forward.

hunks.baseline: Waves spread outward in layers with the violent collision.
hunks.sol: The collision sent waves of force spreading outward, one after another.

hunks.baseline: By the time the shock and thunderous roar that had shaken the world had subsided, the flames that had pulverized every obstacle in their path were also fading away, having exhausted their strength.
hunks.sol: By the time the shock and thunderous roar had subsided, the flames had pulverized every obstacle in their path. Now they, too, were fading, their strength spent.

hunks.baseline: They had ultimately failed to reach the monster’s body, which was disappearing into the thick darkness in the distance.
hunks.sol: The spear had failed to reach the monster before its body vanished into the darkness far ahead.

hunks.baseline: The spear, drifting helplessly with the current, was caught in someone’s hand.
hunks.sol: Someone caught the spear as it drifted helplessly with the current.

hunks.baseline: The back of the man silently staring in the direction the monster had vanished seemed to radiate emotion ready to erupt like an active volcano.
hunks.sol: The man stood with his back to me, staring silently in the direction the monster had gone. He seemed ready to erupt like an active volcano.

hunks.baseline: No, let me correct that.
hunks.sol: No. Let me correct that.

hunks.baseline: It was not merely that he seemed to radiate emotion ready to erupt.
hunks.sol: He didn’t merely *seem* ready to erupt. One touch, and he would explode.

hunks.baseline: It looked as though he would explode if anyone so much as touched him.
Even in that moment, when he had lost the monster that could never be allowed to live.
hunks.sol: He’d been that way when the monster he could never allow to live had escaped.

hunks.baseline: …Even now.
hunks.sol: And he was that way now.

hunks.baseline: The instant the sharp voice slipped from my lips without my realizing it—
hunks.sol: The sharp word escaped my lips before I realized it.

hunks.baseline: Everything that had filled the surroundings melted away in a vivid green light.
The sea, dark as night.
The enormous wreckage left behind by the skyscrapers.
hunks.sol: A vivid green light spread through the water, and everything around me melted away.

hunks.baseline: Even the nameless corpses that had met their deaths with their eyes wide open.
hunks.sol: The sea, dark as night. The enormous wreckage of high-rise buildings. Even the nameless corpses that had died with their eyes wide open.

hunks.baseline: The empty space where the hologram had disappeared was filled by several dozen unfamiliar faces.
hunks.sol: In place of the vanished hologram, several dozen unfamiliar faces came into view.

hunks.baseline: Men dressed in custom-tailored suits and military uniforms that looked expensive at a glance.
hunks.sol: Men in military uniforms and expensive-looking tailored suits.

hunks.baseline: Among them, the old man sitting in the seat of honor across from me opened his mouth with a grim expression.
hunks.sol: The old man seated opposite me, at the head of the table, spoke with a grave expression.

hunks.baseline: “Good heavens. To think Leviathan got away.”
hunks.sol: “To think Leviathan got away.”

hunks.baseline: It was the first time I had seen his face, but according to Team Leader Choi, that old man was one of the three most powerful people in Japan.
hunks.sol: I’d never met him before today, but according to Team Leader Choi, he was one of the three most powerful people in Japan.

hunks.baseline: No—if you counted only the authority he actually possessed, he might even have been number one.
hunks.sol: No—if you counted the authority he actually wielded, he might be number one.

hunks.baseline: The position of Defense Minister was an immensely powerful one even in peacetime. In a situation like this, with the country at war, he possessed more power than anyone.
hunks.sol: Defense Minister was an immensely powerful position even in peacetime. With the country at war, it carried more power than ever.

hunks.baseline: But I was not in a good mood as I looked at the old Defense Minister.
hunks.sol: But looking at the old Defense Minister put me in a foul mood.

hunks.baseline: To be a little more honest, I wanted to deal with that damned old man in front of me before Leviathan, who was not even there right now.
hunks.sol: To be honest, I wanted to deal with that damned old man before Leviathan, who wasn’t even here.

Simple.
hunks.sol: Why? Simple.

hunks.baseline: Because that man had eliminated the last chance of catching Leviathan only an hour ago.
hunks.sol: An hour ago, he’d eliminated our last chance to catch it.

hunks.baseline: Now that I understood the whole situation, there was no way my words could be pleasant.
hunks.sol: Now that I knew what had happened, I wasn’t about to be polite.

hunks.baseline: “Exactly. It was a shame we missed it. If someone had helped us at the end, we might have caught it.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. Shame it got away. If someone had helped at the end, we might have caught it.”

hunks.baseline: The air in the conference room froze in an instant. While the Japanese men glanced around nervously, the Defense Minister glared at me with displeasure.
hunks.sol: The conference room went still. While the other Japanese men glanced nervously at one another, the Defense Minister fixed me with an offended stare.

hunks.baseline: “What you said sounds as though you are implying that Japan is responsible. Did these old ears hear you incorrectly?”
hunks.sol: “That sounds as though you’re blaming Japan. Or have my old ears misheard you?”

hunks.baseline: “I heard you were over eighty, but you still seem remarkably healthy. Your ears work pretty well for an old man.”
hunks.sol: “I heard you were over eighty, but you’re still in good shape. Your hearing’s pretty sharp for an old man.”

hunks.baseline: “What did you say?”
hunks.sol: “What?”

hunks.baseline: “Have your ears actually gotten worse? You already heard me, so why do you keep asking?”
hunks.sol: “Has it suddenly gone bad? You heard me. Why keep asking?”

hunks.baseline: “What kind of—!”
hunks.sol: “How dare—!”

hunks.baseline: The Defense Minister slammed his hand on the table and turned toward Team Leader Choi.
hunks.sol: The Defense Minister slammed the table and turned to Team Leader Choi.

hunks.baseline: “Are you simply going to stand by and watch this insolence?”
hunks.sol: “Are you going to stand there and allow this insolence?”

hunks.baseline: Normally, Team Leader Choi would have given me a warning look around this point.
hunks.sol: Normally, Team Leader Choi would have given me a warning look by now.

hunks.baseline: That is, normally.
hunks.sol: Normally.

hunks.baseline: “When you speak of insolence, Defense Minister, are you perhaps referring to striking the table in a place like this?”
hunks.sol: “By ‘insolence,’ Defense Minister, do you mean striking the table during a meeting like this?”

hunks.baseline: “Japan formally requested assistance through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and we risked our lives to come all the way here in response. And yet…”
hunks.sol: “Japan formally requested assistance through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. We answered that request and risked our lives to come here. And yet…”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi’s words cut off, and his gaze turned cold.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi fell silent. His gaze turned cold.

hunks.baseline: “Why did your side not deploy additional forces?”
hunks.sol: “Why did you not deploy additional forces?”

hunks.baseline: “As I understand it, at the exact moment Jin Taekyung attacked Leviathan, at least two thousand Hunters had been mobilized. The Ground and Air Self-Defense Forces were also standing by.”
hunks.sol: “As I understand it, at least two thousand Hunters had been assembled by the time Jin Taekyung attacked Leviathan. The Ground and Air Self-Defense Forces were standing by as well.”

hunks.baseline: “I know. I know that most of them would not have been much help in battle. But if you had deployed Japan’s Hunters, even at the last moment, they could have delayed the fleeing Leviathan for a little while.”
hunks.sol: “I know most of them would not have been much help in a fight. But if you had deployed Japan’s Hunters, even then, they could have slowed Leviathan’s escape for a little while.”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi’s words were clear and precise. They were also entirely true.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi had laid out the facts clearly.

hunks.baseline: That little bit of time was exactly what I had needed.
hunks.sol: That little while was exactly what I’d needed.

hunks.baseline: A small amount of support and sacrifice to distract the wounded monster dragging its battered body away and make it lose precious time.
hunks.sol: A bit of support—and sacrifice—to distract the wounded monster and delay it as it dragged itself away.

hunks.baseline: But in that deep sea, where I had risked my life to enter, all I could do was watch the monster’s back grow more distant.
hunks.sol: Instead, after risking my life to go down into that deep water, I’d had to watch its back grow smaller in the distance.

hunks.baseline: “I was about to lead the Hunters in myself because I could not stand by and watch, but your side stopped us. You even invoked your authority over field operations.”
hunks.sol: “I could no longer stand by, so I tried to lead the Hunters in myself. Your side stopped us. You even invoked your authority over field operations.”

hunks.baseline: “If you wanted to minimize your own sacrifices and take all the credit, you should have done it properly. Then things would never have reached this point.”
hunks.sol: “If you wanted to keep your own losses down and claim the credit, you should have done the job properly. Then we wouldn’t be in this situation.”

hunks.baseline: The Defense Minister clenched his lips tightly before speaking.
hunks.sol: The Defense Minister pressed his lips together.

hunks.baseline: “The encirclement—the encirclement was perfect.”
hunks.sol: “The encirclement… The encirclement was perfect.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King, who had been listening, asked me with genuine confusion.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King looked at me with genuine curiosity.

hunks.baseline: “If it was perfect, shouldn’t it not have been breached?”
hunks.sol: “If it was perfect, shouldn’t Leviathan have failed to break through?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, exactly.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. It should have.”

hunks.baseline: “But I heard it was breached?”
hunks.sol: “But it broke through?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. It was.”
hunks.sol: “Yep.”

hunks.baseline: “And you even lost its location because of the magical power it released?”
hunks.sol: “And you lost track of it because of the magical power it released?”

hunks.baseline: After listening to all my helpful answers, the Skeleton King muttered,
hunks.sol: Having listened to all my helpful answers, the Skeleton King muttered, “What? Are they fucking idiots…?”

hunks.baseline: “What the hell? Are they idiots…?”
With that single statement striking the truth with perfect accuracy, the temperature inside the conference room dropped below freezing.
hunks.sol: The temperature in the conference room seemed to drop below freezing.

hunks.baseline: But even as I watched everyone clamp their mouths shut and glance nervously at one another, I felt not the slightest bit satisfied.
hunks.sol: But watching everyone fall silent and glance nervously around gave me no satisfaction at all.

hunks.baseline: *What a bunch of fucking lunatics.*
hunks.sol: *Fucking lunatics.*

hunks.baseline: Seeing these bugs, worse than monsters, sitting there pretending to be an operations command center was not even enough to make me laugh bitterly.
hunks.sol: Those bugs were worse than monsters, and they were sitting there calling themselves the operation’s command staff. I couldn’t even laugh.

hunks.baseline: *It’s not like I can call this fucking bullshit and quit, either.*
hunks.sol: *It’s not like I can say “fuck this” and quit.*

hunks.baseline: The number of casualties confirmed so far was roughly one hundred thousand.
hunks.sol: The casualty count so far was roughly a hundred thousand.

hunks.baseline: It was only this low because, fortunately, the tsunami Leviathan had created had stopped around the outskirts of Tokyo.
hunks.sol: It was only that low because, by some stroke of luck, the tsunami Leviathan had caused had stopped around the outskirts of Tokyo.

hunks.baseline: If it returned after I left, Tokyo would be renamed Atlantis.
hunks.sol: If I left and it came back, they might as well rename Tokyo Atlantis.

hunks.baseline: *And if it gives up on Japan and targets somewhere else…*
hunks.sol: *And if it gives up on Japan and goes after somewhere else…*

hunks.baseline: That would be a problem in its own way.
hunks.sol: That would be a problem too.

hunks.baseline: Of course, the idiots—including that old monkey chief standing before me—would probably celebrate and dance with joy just because they had survived.
hunks.sol: Of course, the idiots here—including that old monkey chief—would probably dance for joy because *they’d* survived.

hunks.baseline: They were exactly the kind of people who would do that.
hunks.sol: The worst part was, they really would.

hunks.baseline: The thought only made me feel worse.
After letting out a hundred-percent pure, deep sigh, I spoke to the Defense Minister, who had become completely silent.
hunks.sol: I let out a sigh of pure, undiluted exasperation and addressed the Defense Minister, who had finally shut his mouth.

hunks.baseline: “Enough with the pointless arguing. Call someone else in charge.”
hunks.sol: “Enough. Get me someone else in charge.”

hunks.baseline: “S-Someone else in charge?”
hunks.sol: “S-someone else?”

hunks.baseline: “The Prime Minister. Or the King of Japan. Anyone has to be better than you.”
hunks.sol: “The Prime Minister. Or the King of Japan. Whoever it is, they’ll be better than you.”

hunks.baseline: “The King of Japan?! How dare you refer to His Majesty the Emperor of the Great Japanese Empire that way—”
hunks.sol: “The King of Japan? How dare you speak of His Majesty the Emperor of the Great Japanese Empire—”

hunks.baseline: “This is driving me crazy. How long are you going to keep using that empire crap? If you collapsed after taking two atomic bombs, you should have surrendered the title of Emperor too. Don’t you think?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, give me a break. How long are you going to keep up the empire crap? Your empire got flattened by two atomic bombs. You should’ve given up the title of Emperor while you were at it.”

hunks.baseline: “That was a savage and barbaric act of destruction by those American Yankees!”
hunks.sol: “That was a savage act of destruction by the American Yankees!”

hunks.baseline: I covered my ears as the Defense Minister screamed.
hunks.sol: I plugged my ears as the Defense Minister shrieked.

hunks.baseline: “I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning.”
hunks.sol: “I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I’m going to get radiation poisoning.”

hunks.baseline: Was it because he had already lived a full life? Or had radiation contamination robbed him of his fear?
hunks.sol: Maybe he’d lived long enough not to care. Or maybe radiation contamination had robbed him of all fear.

hunks.baseline: Just as the Defense Minister was rampaging and charging at me with his old body, the Skeleton King reached out and seized him by the back of the neck.
hunks.sol: As the Defense Minister charged at me, flailing despite his age, the Skeleton King reached out and caught him by the back of the neck.

hunks.baseline: “Stop, you old and insignificant per—no, Yellow Monkey.”
hunks.sol: “Stop, you old and insignificant hu—no, Yellow Monkey.”

hunks.baseline: “You insolent dog! Release me at once! How dare a Yankee bastard covered in fur lay his hands on the Defense Minister of the Great Japanese Empire!”
hunks.sol: “You wretch! Release me at once! How dare a fur-covered Yankee lay a hand on the Defense Minister of the Great Japanese Empire!”

hunks.baseline: “Do you dare insult the mighty United States in front of me?”
hunks.sol: “You dare insult the great United States in front of me?”

hunks.baseline: “I have not forgotten! I have not forgotten the terrible things you bastards did to this land and its innocent subjects of the Imperial State!”
hunks.sol: “I have not forgotten what you bastards did to this land and the innocent subjects of our empire!”

hunks.baseline: *What the hell are these lunatics…*
hunks.sol: *These fucking lunatics…*

hunks.baseline: A heated argument between a Japanese imperialist from the ’70s–’80s generation and an American monster from the Demon Realm.
hunks.sol: A Japanese imperialist from the ’70s-and-’80s generation arguing with an American monster from the Demon Realm.

hunks.baseline: Watching those horrifying hybrids with my own two eyes made my chest swell with emotion despite itself, but it was not over yet.
hunks.sol: The sight of those two horrifying oddities made my chest swell with emotion. Unfortunately, it wasn’t over.

hunks.baseline: What the hell was this?
hunks.sol: What the hell?

hunks.baseline: My entire body suddenly grew cold, and the fluorescent lights began to dim.
hunks.sol: A chill ran through me, and the fluorescent lights began to dim.

hunks.baseline: Even the people struggling desperately to pull the Defense Minister and the Skeleton King apart felt the chill and shuddered.
hunks.sol: Even the people struggling to separate the Defense Minister and the Skeleton King shuddered in the cold.

hunks.baseline: *What the hell is happening all of a sudden?*
hunks.sol: *What’s happening now?*

hunks.baseline: I turned my head in confusion.
In midair, my eyes met Team Leader Choi’s.
hunks.sol: I turned my head. My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s across the room.

hunks.baseline: And in that moment, I realized something and stood there with my mouth hanging open.
hunks.sol: That was when I realized it. My mouth fell open.

hunks.baseline: In my ears, someone’s shout from a moment earlier was repeating itself with vivid clarity.
hunks.sol: A shout from moments earlier rang through my ears again.

hunks.baseline: *No, fuck. Don’t tell me…*
hunks.sol: *No. Fuck. Don’t tell me…*

hunks.baseline: The eerie energy transformed into a gale and shattered the fluorescent lights on the ceiling.
hunks.sol: The eerie energy became a gale, shattering the fluorescent lights overhead.

hunks.baseline: I was already running through the sudden darkness toward someone.
hunks.sol: I was already running through the sudden darkness toward the Skeleton King.

hunks.baseline: “Look closely, and feel the resentment of the—”
hunks.sol: “Look closely, and feel their resentment—!”

hunks.baseline: Thanks to a traditional promotion system that still prioritized family and connections over ability even in the twenty-first century, most of the high-ranking officials and generals inside the conference room were ordinary people. They were so frightened that they had not even heard the Skeleton King’s shout.
hunks.sol: Thanks to a time-honored promotion system that still valued family and connections over ability in the twenty-first century, most of the high-ranking officials and generals in the conference room were ordinary people. They were too frightened even to hear the Skeleton King’s shout.

hunks.baseline: And apparently my demand to call someone in charge had gotten through, because not long afterward, the manager—no, the Prime Minister—arrived.
hunks.sol: And apparently my demand for someone in charge had gotten through. Before long, the manager—no, the Prime Minister—arrived.

hunks.baseline: “Thank you so much for coming all the way here to help our homeland, Jinsang!”
hunks.sol: “You came all this way to help our country! I am most grateful, Jinsang!”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, yes. It’s nice to meet you, Prime Minister Koizumi.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, yes. Nice to meet you, Prime Minister Koizumi.”

hunks.baseline: I had never imagined I would live to see the day I met this man in person.
hunks.sol: I never thought I’d meet this man in person.

hunks.baseline: I had always seen collections of his famous quotes on the internet, so meeting him like this briefly made me feel as if I had run into a celebrity.
hunks.sol: I’d only ever seen collections of his quotes online. Seeing him now gave me a brief jolt of excitement, like I’d met a celebrity.

hunks.baseline: Of course, given the situation, I could not show it. The important matter right now was Leviathan.
hunks.sol: Of course, this wasn’t the time to show it. We needed to deal with Leviathan.

hunks.baseline: At the very least, that was what I wanted.
hunks.sol: At least, that was what I wanted to do.

hunks.baseline: I wanted to.
hunks.sol: *I* did.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll get straight to the point. In order to track Leviathan—”
hunks.sol: “I’ll get straight to the point. To track Leviathan—”

hunks.baseline: “I heard the Defense Minister was rude to you, Jinsang. Once this matter is settled, I will severely reprimand him, if only to soothe your feelings!”
hunks.sol: “I hear the Defense Minister was rude to you, Jinsang. Once this is over, I shall reprimand him severely, if only to ease your hurt feelings!”

hunks.baseline: “Uh, wow. I really appreciate that.”
hunks.sol: “Uh. Thanks. I appreciate it.”

hunks.baseline: “Why do you look like that, Jinsang?”
hunks.sol: “Why the look, Jinsang?”

hunks.baseline: “No, it’s just… We also need to discuss Leviathan. And the way you keep addressing me is a little…”
hunks.sol: “It’s just… We need to talk about Leviathan. And there’s the way you keep addressing me.”

hunks.baseline: “What is wrong with the way I address you, Jinsang?”
hunks.sol: “The way I address you, Jinsang?”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, I see. It must sound different in Korea. Then shall I call you Gyeongsang, using the last syllable of your name?”
hunks.sol: “Ah, I see. It must sound like something else in Korean. Then shall I call you Gyeongsang, using the last syllable of your name?”

hunks.baseline: There was no way that would work.
hunks.sol: How would that help?

hunks.baseline: I felt as though I had dodged a pile of shit only to get pissed on.
hunks.sol: I’d dodged a pile of shit only to get pissed on.

hunks.baseline: *Is he wishing me a minor injury the next time I fight Leviathan…?*
hunks.sol: *Is he wishing me a minor injury next time I fight Leviathan…?*

hunks.baseline: I seriously considered Jinsang versus Gyeongsang, then sighed.
hunks.sol: I weighed Jinsang against Gyeongsang, then sighed.
